advisory.finding: `_start_gate_job` now calls `config.repo_root()` outside any try/except, after `begin_gate_job` has already reserved a leader slot in the in-flight registry. If root resolution raises (for example `FileNotFoundError` when the cwd has been deleted and `REBAR_ROOT` is unset, a raise documented as intentional), no daemon is spawned and `handle.complete()` is never called. The reserved entry stays active, so duplicate starts attach to a job that will never run, and `gate_run_status` keeps reporting `attaching`. Before this change the same resolution happened inside `gate_runs`' `try: ... except OSError` blocks, which swallowed the error, and the daemon still ran and settled the handle.
scenarios: MCP server process whose cwd has been removed and which has no REBAR_ROOT set: the first `*_start` raises after it has reserved the dedup slot, and every later identical start attaches to a job that never runs
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_start_gate_job`, compute `root = str(config.repo_root())` before calling `begin_gate_job` and pass `repo_root=root` to `begin_gate_job` too, so basis resolution and the run index use the same root. A resolution failure then raises before any registry entry exists.

New test assertions: `assert record and record["status"] == "passed"` and `assert not (other / ".rebar" / "gate_runs").exists()`. Neither looks at `gate_runs.owner_lock_path(job_id, repo_root=str(store))`.
The commit message says the bug covered 'owner lock, running and terminal records, lock release', but only the record writes are checked.
advisory.finding: The new regression test never checks that the owner-lock release uses the pinned root. If `gate_runs.release_owner_lock(owner_lock, handle.job_id, repo_root=root)` lost its `repo_root=root`, the unlink would target `<other>/.rebar/gate_runs/<job_id>.lock`, which doesn't exist (the call ignores OSError, so it fails silently). The lock file would then stay in the starting store. The test would still pass, because it only checks the record status and that `other/.rebar/gate_runs` doesn't exist, and unlink never creates that directory.
scenarios: Someone later drops `repo_root=root` from the release_owner_lock call (or adds a new write that ignores it). The lock file leaks into the starting store whenever REBAR_ROOT/cwd changes mid-gate, and the suite stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the status loop, add a bounded poll: `while time.monotonic() < deadline and gate_runs.owner_lock_path(handle["job_id"], repo_root=str(store)).exists(): time.sleep(0.02)`, then `assert not gate_runs.owner_lock_path(handle["job_id"], repo_root=str(store)).exists()`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In _start_gate_job, look up the root before begin_gate_job reserves the slot, or wrap the lookup at line 308 so that any failure calls handle.complete(error=exc) (or keeps the old best-effort behaviour) and no unsettled leader entry is left behind.
evidence: Primary failure: config.repo_root() falls back to Path.cwd(), which RAISES FileNotFoundError via os.getcwd() when the working directory has been deleted (src/rebar/_config_sources.py:61-64, 76).

Old path: every place this lookup happened before was best-effort. begin_gate_job's basis lookup catches every exception and returns an 'unresolved:<ref>' value (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:69-74). hold_owner_lock calls `_index_dir(repo_root)` inside `try ... except OSError` and returns None (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:125-131). record_gate_run catches OSError and only logs it (src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:97-102). The daemon still started, and its finally block always called handle.complete (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:267).

Old surfaced result: the start call returned {job_id, status:'running'}. The job then finished as passed or failed, and _finish purged the dedup key (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:184-188), so a later start became a new leader and launched a fresh run.

New path: `root = str(config.repo_root())` at src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:308 runs outside any try block, after begin_gate_job has registered the leader entry (src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:294-305; _attach_or_create stores it at src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:172-174).
New surfaced result: an uncaught FileNotFoundError from the *_start tool. No daemon is spawned, so handle.complete is never called and the registry entry stays `done=False`.

Caller that changes behaviour: a retried *_start with the same key hits `if hit is not None and not hit.done: return hit, False` (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:170-171). It gets is_new=False and the job_id of a job that never started, and launches nothing. is_job_active also keeps reporting that job as active (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:135-141). This lasts until the _MAX_AGE_SECONDS sweep (src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py:144-149).
advisory.finding: When the working directory has been deleted and REBAR_ROOT is unset, the new root lookup at _start_gate_job line 308 raises FileNotFoundError after begin_gate_job has already reserved the leader slot, and nothing catches it. The store-write failure that used to be logged and absorbed now escapes the start tool, and the dedup entry is never settled. Retries then attach to a job that was never started instead of launching a new run.
scenarios: An MCP server whose working directory was deleted (for example a removed worktree or tmp dir), with REBAR_ROOT unset, receives review_plan_start: the call errors, and every retry within the max-age window returns 'running' for a job that never ran.
advisory.suggested_fix: Move `root = str(config.repo_root())` above the `begin_gate_job(...)` call (and pass `repo_root=root` into it as well), so a failed lookup raises before any dedup slot exists. Alternatively, wrap lines 308-320 in try/except BaseException that calls `handle.complete(error=exc)` before re-raising.
